result:
Post revisions are in place, and `pnpm typecheck` passes. I did not boot the app or hit the routes over HTTP, since the task only requires typecheck.

Every successful edit now keeps the pre-save title, excerpt and body as a row in a new `post_revisions` table. The migration was generated with `void db generate`. The revisions page is at `pages/posts/[id]/revisions.tsx`, with a loader that returns `revisions` newest first. Restore is a `POST` server route at `routes/posts/[id]/revisions/[revisionId]/restore.ts`. It snapshots the current version, then writes the chosen revision back, both in one `db.batch`. Both routes redirect guests to `/login` and return 403 for non-authors. A revision that belongs to another post returns 404. Deleting a post also deletes its revisions. The post page shows a Revisions link to authors only.

Two things to know:
- The existing `DELETE` action on a post still has no author check, so any signed-in user can delete any post. I left that unchanged because the task didn't ask for it, but it is a real hole.
- The new migration is generated but not applied to any local database yet. Run `void db migrate` (or `void db reset`) before exercising the app.
